clue.text: Edifice with strong beams

parts.note: beams suggest timber joists holding up a building, but here they are powerful rays of light shone out to sea from a coastal tower

explanation.surface: A building held up by sturdy timber joists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong beams' reads as structural timber; the beams are really light beams warning ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower is a building whose lamp sends out powerful rays to guide shipping.

clue.text: Survive, after all

definitions.meaning: coming after all the others, at the very end

explanation.surface: Managing to survive in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to keep going, and the final one comes after all the rest.

clue.text: Is it taught by the worldly-wise?

definitions.text: Is it taught by the worldly-wise?

parts.words: Is it taught by the worldly-wise?
parts.note: worldly-wise means experienced, but here it means wise about the world, its countries and landscapes

explanation.surface: Asking whether experienced people pass on some lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worldly-wise' means sophisticated; taken literally it means knowing about the world, as a school subject teacher does.
explanation.definitionFit: The school subject studying the Earth's lands, peoples and features.

clue.text: Model requests jobs

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A fashion model asks for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests fashion; it gives T from the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties or pieces of work to be done.

clue.text: Given command, other ranks run into action

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the letter for run goes into the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Soldiers are given the command and rush into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Told to do something by someone in authority.

clue.text: Ten sons out to get fourteen liners

indicators.note: the letters of ten sons are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten boys go out to fetch a set of fourteen ocean liners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourteen liners' looks like ships; it means poems of fourteen lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Poems of fourteen lines, as written by Shakespeare and Petrarch.

clue.text: Getting married in a church will be a high spot

indicators.note: the letter for married goes inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church wedding will be the high point of someone's life.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak or summit, the highest point of achievement.

clue.text: Accounts love this chocolate supplier

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for current account, so two of them stand for the plural
love means nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Bookkeepers adore this cocoa merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chocolate supplier' sounds like a firm; it is the tree whose seeds give cocoa.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical tree whose beans are ground to make cocoa.

clue.text: Forms to be filled at a general election

definitions.text: Forms to be filled at a general election

parts.words: Forms to be filled at a general election
parts.note: forms suggests paperwork, but a form is also a bench, and vacant places in parliament are filled by voting

explanation.surface: Paperwork to complete when voting nationally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms to be filled' suggests paperwork; a form is also a bench, and vacant parliamentary places are filled by voting.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant places, here parliamentary constituencies awaiting members chosen by voters.

clue.text: Person who lives here will dislike having to carry id

indicators.note: the word for dislike holds the letters of id inside it

parts.note: to resent is to dislike bitterly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local will resent being made to carry identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has a home in a particular place.

clue.text: Do they punctuate the bus route?

definitions.text: Do they punctuate the bus route?

parts.words: Do they punctuate the bus route?
parts.note: punctuation marks such as full points and the places where a bus halts along its way share one name

explanation.surface: Wondering what breaks up a bus's journey at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punctuate' is used in its sense of interrupting at intervals, while also hinting at full points in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Halting places along a bus route, and also full points in punctuation.

clue.text: Top gear when going into a corner?

definitions.text: Top gear when going into a corner?

parts.words: Top gear when going into a corner?
parts.note: top gear sounds like motoring, but it is headwear, a pointed hat once put on a slow pupil sent to stand in the corner

explanation.surface: A driver asks whether to stay in the highest gear through a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' and 'corner' suggest driving; the hat was a classroom punishment, worn while standing in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical paper hat formerly placed on a slow pupil made to stand in a classroom corner.

clue.text: Pickle, perhaps, specially for game

definitions.meaning: pickle is one example of jam-like food kept in a jar
an area of land kept specially for game animals and birds

explanation.surface: A pickle made especially to go with game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is one kind of bottled food kept from spoiling, and a game reserve is land set aside for wild animals.

clue.text: Sarcasm from the club youth leader

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, taken here from youth

explanation.surface: Sarcastic remarks from the leader of a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club youth leader' reads as one person in charge of a youth club; club is a golf iron instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockery that says the opposite of what is meant, close kin to sarcasm.

clue.text: St Michael's arranged to see those seeking the elixir of life

definitions.text: those seeking the elixir of life

indicators.note: the letters of St Michael's, including the final s, are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A church named for an archangel is laid out for questers after eternal life.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Michael's counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval experimenters sought both gold from base metal and a potion granting eternal youth.

clue.text: Watch what one says

parts.note: the phrase usually means be careful in speech, but here it means literally to observe a speaker's mouth to follow the words

explanation.surface: A warning to be careful about one's words.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means 'be careful what you say'; read literally, it is following speech by watching the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people may understand speech by watching the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Travel overseas to get home

parts.note: reads as returning home from abroad, but it means going abroad to find a new home there

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses the sea to return home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get home' suggests returning; it means settling in a new home abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's own country to settle permanently in another.

clue.text: She is given two articles set in a case

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article and the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article and the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A woman is handed two items to pack into a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests objects; it means the grammatical words 'a' and 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade into its scabbard or sleeve-like holder.

clue.text: Score a single was the key to opening in the old days

definitions.text: the key to opening in the old days

parts.note: a score is twenty
a single means one

explanation.surface: A single notch on the scoreboard was once the clue to unlocking something.
explanation.walkthrough: Traditionally a young person was given the key of the door on coming of age at this age.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming of age once happened at this birthday, marked by handing over the key of the door.

clue.text: We get involved with hairy bats

indicators.note: the letters of we and hairy become tangled together and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: We tangle with hairy flying mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the creatures, but it is the definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for mad, and something gone wild or out of control is crazy.

clue.text: Clamp down in French legion

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a legion is a military force

explanation.surface: A crackdown within the French Foreign Legion.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose a law strictly, as one does in a crackdown.

clue.text: Monastery bugle-call?

definitions.meaning: a monastery is a place of quiet withdrawal from the world
the military signal sounded at sunset or to order a withdrawal

explanation.surface: A bugle sounding in a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious house serves as a place of seclusion, and a military signal at sunset bears the same name.

clue.text: Screen has crimson centre and unusual rose edging

indicators.note: the word for crimson goes in the centre of the rearranged letters
the rearranged letters of rose form the edges around the colour word
unusual means the letters of rose are put in an odd order

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A screen with a crimson middle and an odd border of roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' turns ROSE into RE...OS, and 'centre' and 'edging' put RED in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental partition behind a church altar.

clue.text: It's held at the back, by gum

definitions.text: It's held at the back, by gum

parts.words: It's held at the back, by gum
parts.note: by gum sounds like a mild northern exclamation, but it means held in place by the gums at the rear of the mouth

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise about something kept at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum' is an old exclamation of surprise; read literally, it means held by the gum, as a back tooth is.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad grinding tooth near the back of the jaw, rooted in the gum.

clue.text: Don't get up early — about one is right

indicators.note: the word for a legal right goes around the letter for one

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to stay in bed, said to be correct at about one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in bed past the usual hour of rising.

clue.text: Loses a game

definitions.meaning: gives up something as a penalty
a parlour game in which players pay penalties for mistakes

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up something as a penalty, and a party pastime in which players redeem pledged items.

clue.text: Hail trapped between two points of roof projection

indicators.note: the word for hail is caught between the two compass letters

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south
ave is the Latin greeting meaning hail

explanation.surface: Hailstones caught between two spikes of a roof overhang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather; it is the greeting AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The overhanging lower edge of a roof.

clue.text: Unlikely to run quickly

definitions.meaning: colourfast dye will not run in the wash

explanation.surface: Someone who is unlikely to run fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dye that holds colour without running, and moving at speed.

clue.text: Yet civilians lived such a life in the war

definitions.text: Yet civilians lived such a life in the war

parts.words: Yet civilians lived such a life in the war
parts.note: a protected, comfortable life, yet in wartime civilians literally lived in air-raid refuges

explanation.surface: A comment that even wartime civilians led a protected life.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a cosseted life is also literal: civilians spent nights in air-raid refuges.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected life is one kept from hardship, and wartime civilians took cover in bomb refuges.

clue.text: Instrument played in "twelfth night"

definitions.meaning: a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin
the heroine of Shakespeare's comedy, a role an actress plays

explanation.surface: An instrument heard in a performance of Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' suggests music, but it means a part acted: the heroine of Twelfth Night shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument pitched below the violin, and the shipwrecked heroine of Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Castle building material

parts.note: suggests stone for a fortress, but it is what children use to build castles on the beach

explanation.surface: What a fortress is built from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castle' suggests stone; the castle is a child's one on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Children build little castles on the beach from damp grains of the shore.

clue.text: It's present in a constantly recurring form

indicators.note: the letters of it's and present are put into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that is always there in a repeating shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' signals the anagram; 'in a' joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps happening again and again without letting up.
